analysis: What changed vs the 8 AM brief: the rally strengthened rather than fading. Barron's late-morning read has the Nasdaq +1.6%, the S&P +1.2% and the Dow +503 points in the first two hours — a step up from the 9:46 AM ET prints (+0.64%/+0.77%/+0.69%) — and, notably, with no clear catalyst: Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid calls it the tech selloff stabilising and risk appetite returning. The day's arc is now a round trip for Nvidia: it opened at $151.90, fell to a $145.39 low, and has clawed back to $149.15 (-0.10%) at 11:52 AM ET, essentially flat vs Wednesday's $149.30 close. The leadership has rotated while NVDA stalls — Tesla +4.8%, Amazon +3.8% and Meta +3.5% carry the tape, and AMD is +2.4% despite a fresh Erste Group downgrade to Hold, which reads as the market discounting valuation worries against strong Q3 numbers ($13.4B revenue, +45% y/y). Signal vs noise: the broadening of the rally beyond Nvidia and the late-morning strengthening on a 3.5-hour session are signal — the rebound has follow-through now, just not from its usual leader. The Banks/Warren and Megaspeed underreporting items remain single-source and unconfirmed, so they stay escalation risk rather than fact. Gold (+3.4%) and silver (+6%) ripping alongside stocks is still the odd pairing to watch — hedging demand running with risk-on, not against it. The 1 PM ET close is the next test on thin holiday volume.

headlines.headline: The rally strengthened into late morning: the Nasdaq is +1.6%, the S&P 500 +1.2% and the Dow +503 points (+1%) in the first two hours of trading, per Barron's — up from the 9:46 AM ET prints of +0.77%/+0.64%/+0.69%. Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid: 'the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and risk appetite is returning.' No single catalyst was cited.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound is gaining follow-through into the half-day close instead of fading — breadth is widening while the usual leader stalls, which is what a durable bounce looks like.

headlines.headline: Nvidia has clawed back to flat: $149.15 (-0.10%) as of 11:52 AM ET per Finnhub, after opening at $151.90 and dipping to a $145.39 intraday low — essentially back at Wednesday's $149.30 close. Earnings context: Q3 FY2027 reported Nov 17, EPS $2.68 on revenue $115.844B.
headlines.why_it_matters: The morning reversal in the rebound's lead name has been erased — Nvidia is no longer the drag it was at mid-morning, which removes the cap on the Nasdaq's gain.

headlines.headline: Tesla leads the megacaps late morning at $398.23 (+4.8%), with Amazon $253.70 (+3.8%) and Meta $631.42 (+3.5%) close behind; Apple $358.45 (+0.8%), Microsoft flat at $489.70 and Alphabet $272.20 (-0.3%) lag. Anthropic +2.6%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Leadership has rotated to Tesla, Amazon and Meta while Nvidia stalls — the rally is being carried by the rest of the group, which is broader and healthier than a one-stock bounce.

headlines.headline: Erste Group downgraded AMD to Hold from Buy today, citing a valuation well above the sector average and limited near-term upside amid AI-sector uncertainty — but AMD shares are +2.4% at $415.84, shrugging off the call. Earnings context: Q3 revenue $13.4B (+45% y/y) beat the $13.1B estimate; data-center revenue hit a record $8.55B (+97% y/y).
headlines.why_it_matters: A valuation downgrade landing on a day the stock still rises 2.4% says buyers are discounting the call — the downgrade is a sentiment headwind, not a price driver today.

headlines.headline: Black Friday spending reads stay strong: ICSC reports in-store shopping is expected to reach its highest level since 2019, with 84% of American shoppers visiting stores in person; Adobe forecasts $12.9B in online spending today (+9.2% y/y) and $15.1B on Cyber Monday (+6.2%).
headlines.why_it_matters: A strong in-store turnout plus a near-double-digit online gain is the first real demand read for consumer names — it supports the retail leg of the rally if the actual tally matches.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning; shares $23.95 (+2.26%) at 11:51 AM ET per Finnhub (open $23.94, high $24.10, low $23.76, prev close $23.42), riding the broad rally. Carry-forward: Q3 2026 (Nov 3) revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y) beat the ~$344.7M consensus and adjusted EPS $0.33 beat the $0.26 consensus; adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M and DCF to $495-505M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6. Leverage 3.78x, near the 3.75x target; $600M of 6.75% senior notes due 2035 issued in September. Zacks raised FY2026 EPS estimate to $1.16 from $1.04 (Nov 24) and holds a Hold rating; a Nov 24 Zacks piece frames the growth case — $500M order book through 2029, >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted, record $23.14/month revenue per horsepower (+8% y/y) — while a Nov 26 Seeking Alpha Hold note counters with limited upside at 8.29x forward EV/EBITDA amid substantial debt, against a Nov 25 buy-rated piece at $23.63 citing the 8.9% yield and 1.67x coverage. USAC opened Wednesday at $23.04. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.
